analysis.title: Retail Radar Oct 7 – Seasonally stronger, Tech back in focus
key_insights: Retail flows were $5.7B for Oct 1-7, below the 12-month average of $6.7B/week. ETFs took +$4.7B and single stocks +$1.0B. Flows have rebounded from September lows back to roughly their 12-month average levels.
ETF flows recovered from depressed levels to the 32nd percentile. Single-name flows alternated between buying and selling and closed the week at the 43rd percentile.

Retail inflows into Tech sector ETFs rose to the 73rd percentile, from the 4th percentile four weeks ago. Mag 7 flows stayed resilient. Tech ex Mag 7 strengthened, led by SNDK and MU (3rd and 4th most bought stocks last week).

Retail investors were net buyers across Tech this week: Semis, Hardware and also Software. Tech single stocks drew +$602M, Industrials +$143M. Communications (-$231M), Financials (-$184M), Health Care (-$153M) and Materials (-$120M) saw net selling.
Mag 7 retail activity: NVDA +$834M, GOOG/L +$265M, TSLA +$122M, AMZN +$81M, MSFT +$34M, META +$4M, AAPL -$15M.

SPCX (SpaceX) was reported to be seeking to raise $40B to buy NVDA chips. The stock rose 15% last week while retail investors sold $177M, trimming the large position built after the IPO. The pace of selling slowed in October.

The S&P 500 hit record highs on Tuesday and re-evaluated the next day on rising yields, geopolitical risk and oil volatility. JPM's US business cycle indicator remains strong, lifted by its growth component.
The weakest retail seasonality period (Q3) appears to be behind. Retail seasonality is typically strongest in January and weakest in Q3, and the data so far supports that pattern.
ETF flows rebounded across Broad-Based, Style and Fixed Income ETFs, except Commodity and Crypto ETFs. International ETF activity was minimal despite volatility in France and Brazil.

Retail investors accelerated selling of IGOV (-3.0z). IGOV's allocation to French bonds is its second largest after Japan. JPM's view is that French bond weakness reflects a technical unwind of carry trades and real-money hedging more than 2027 fiscal or political uncertainty.

MSCI Brazil rallied 13% Monday after Flavio Bolsonaro overtook Lula in the first round of the Brazilian election. JPM strategists see a further 20% gain in the short term, with forward P/E re-rating about 20-25% to 11x from 8.8x. They are most constructive on rate-sensitive stocks, and expect stocks that benefit from a weaker BRL to underperform.
Retail investors largely ignored the EWZ rally ($6.6M sold over 3 days, -1.3z) and sold most Brazilian ADRs: NU, PBR, ABEV, BBD, STNE, XP. ITUB was the exception, with $13.7M bought (4.1z).

September momentum was strong on both legs. The top 20 Momentum names rose about 12% (top 30: +10%), led by Semiconductors with support from Health Care and Energy. The top 100 was roughly flat. The bottom 100 fell about 11% and the bottom 20 about 12%.
Crowding in Laggards fell to the 17th-20th percentile from about the 47th percentile at the end of August. Retail activity in Momentum ETFs resumed, with buying in SPMO and XMMO and selling in MTUM.

3Q earnings season starts Tuesday. Consensus expects earnings growth of +31% y/y (+27% ex-Energy) and revenue growth of +12% y/y (+11% ex-Energy). Energy and Technology lead, Staples lag. FY26 revisions have trended lower since early September.

About 5% of S&P 500 market cap reports in the next 7 days, mostly Financials. JPM analysts see room for a pre-earnings bounce in large banks after recent underperformance, backed by better net interest income expectations as rate-hike pricing rose, and likely stronger trading revenue. Retail has shown few signs of buying the weakness in XLF or bank stocks.

GOOGL and CEG announced a clean energy collaboration with a 20-year PPA bringing 890MW of new nuclear capacity onto PJM and a 15-year supply agreement for 2,700MW. CEG rose about 17% on 10/6. CEG also signed a 20-year PPA with AMZN for 690MW at Calvert Cliffs last week.
VST surged 15% Monday on reports the US Administration plans a roughly $4.2B loan package to upgrade three nuclear plants. META has 20-year power purchase agreements with Vistra plants.

Schneider Electric agreed to acquire PTC for $205 per share in cash, valuing PTC equity at about $22.6B and EV at about $23.7B, roughly 21x 2027E EBITA or 13x with full synergies. PTC jumped 33% Monday.

CHRW fell 11% on 10/5 after agreeing to acquire RXO. JPM analysts are confident in the $300M net cost synergy target but expect revenue dis-synergies to remain a chief concern, a process that could take over a year if the deal closes in 1H27.

SNPS investor day: targets about 15% FY26-FY30E revenue CAGR and about 50% operating margin by FY30E versus about 41.5% guided for FY26E. JPM sees about $35 of earnings power by FY30E. SNPS targets returning up to 50% of FCF and announced a $1.0B buyback authorization.
Retail options trading share is off its highs, with the rolling 1M average at the 92.2nd percentile. Most traded options: TSLA, NVDA, MU, AMD, META, AMZN, SNDK, SPCX, GOOG/L, AAPL.
Futures traders (non-retail) net bought about $0.6B last week, with ES +$2.1B offset by NQ -$1.3B and RTY -$0.2B.

market_movers.rationale: Shares fell 11% on the RXO acquisition. JPM is confident in the $300M cost synergies but flags revenue dis-synergies as a chief concern. Price target of $198 set 05-Oct-26 from $225.
Neutral with $205 target, matching the Schneider Electric cash offer. The stock jumped 33% on the deal.
Moved from Underweight to Neutral on 06-Oct-26 with a $30 target, after the CHRW acquisition agreement.
Schneider Electric moved from Overweight to Neutral on 06-Oct-26 with a €310 target, down from €345.

sector_views.rationale: Large banks could bounce into earnings after underperformance, on better net interest income expectations and likely stronger trading revenue.
Retail demand has returned, with Tech ETF inflows at the 73rd percentile. Consensus has Tech leading 3Q earnings growth along with Energy.
Strategists see MSCI Brazil gaining a further 20% in the short term as forward P/E re-rates to 11x, favoring rate-sensitive stocks.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 S&P 500 consensus earnings growth is +31% y/y (+27% ex-Energy), including private investments. These are consensus estimates, not reported results.
3Q26 consensus revenue growth is +12% y/y (+11% ex-Energy). All sectors are expected to grow earnings faster than in 3Q25, led by Energy and Technology, with Staples weakest.
FY26 earnings revisions have trended lower since early September.
BAC, MS, GS, WFC and C report early next week. Retail flows into them last week: BAC +$5.2M, GS +$12.5M, C +$1M, MS -$4.8M, WFC -$8.8M.
SNPS targets about 15% FY26-FY30E revenue CAGR, about 50% operating margin by FY30E (vs about 41.5% guided for FY26E) and about $35 of EPS power by FY30E.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Consensus expects broad earnings improvement led by Energy and Technology.
Revenue growth is expected to be solid across sectors.

macro_indicators.indicator: US Quant Macro Index growth component
macro_indicators.interpretation: The JPM business cycle indicator is strong, driven by growth. Liquidity is at the 93rd percentile, inflation at the 83rd and sentiment at the 58th.
Higher rate-hike pricing improves net interest income expectations for large banks.

crypto_views: Retail ETF flows rebounded across categories except Commodity and Crypto ETFs.
MSTR, IREN, WULF and NBIS appear on the social media screen with high short interest (MSTR 9.0%, IREN 21.1%, WULF 34.0%, NBIS 21.2% of float).
risk_factors: Rising yields, geopolitical risk and oil volatility drove the S&P 500 off its record high.
FY26 earnings revisions have been trending lower since early September.
Retail not buying weakness in financials ahead of bank earnings.
CHRW/RXO revenue dis-synergies could take over a year to resolve.
Squeeze risk or retail losses in high short interest names with opposite retail and hedge fund positioning.
SPCX Starship flight 14 had a booster engine issue and a second engine failed to reignite during the simulated ocean landing.
vol_and_positioning: Retail options trading share is off its highs, with the rolling 1M average at the 92.2nd percentile.

Meme screen: WULF (34.0% short interest, +2.7z retail imbalance), NBIS (21.2%, +2.5z), IREN (21.1%, +1.3z) and ASTS (34.2%, -1.1z) show opposite positioning between retail and hedge fund shorting, which raises squeeze risk or retail losses.
Crowding in Laggards fell to the 17th-20th percentile from about the 47th at end of August.
Futures traders net bought about $0.6B: ES +$2.1B, NQ -$1.3B, RTY -$0.2B.
KURA short interest is about 18% of float, PVLA about 25%, CABO about 20%.
geopolitical: Flavio Bolsonaro overtook Lula in the first round of the Brazilian election, prompting a 13% rally in MSCI Brazil.
French bond weakness and selective intra-EMU spread contagion, which JPM attributes to a technical unwind of carry trades.
Geopolitical risk and fluctuating oil prices were cited as factors in the S&P 500 pulling back from Tuesday's record high.
